1.contenido: 1. Catechesis has always been considered by the Church as one of its primary tasks, since the risen Christ, before returning to the Father, gave the Apostles this last command: to make disciples of all people, teaching them to observe everything that He had commanded. He thus entrusted them with the mission and the power to announce to men what they themselves had heard, seen with their eyes, contemplated and touched with their hands, about the Word of life. At the same time he entrusted them with the mission and the power to explain with authority what he had taught them, his words and his actions, his signs and his commandments. And he gave them the Spirit to fulfill this mission.

2.contenido: 2. The latest Popes have reserved a prominent place for him in their pastoral concern. My venerated Predecessor Paul VI served the catechesis of the Church in a particularly exemplary manner with his gestures, his preaching, his authoritative interpretation of the Second Vatican Council – which he considered the great catechesis of modern times – with his entire life. He approved, on March 18, 1971, the "General Directory of Catechesis", prepared by the Holy Congregation for the Clergy, a Directory that remains a basic document to guide and stimulate catechetical renewal throughout the Church. He established the International Commission on Catechesis in 1975. He masterfully defined the role and meaning of catechesis in the life and mission of the Church when he addressed the participants in the First International Congress of Catechesis on September 25, 1971, and he explicitly discussed this topic in the Apostolic Exhortation Evangelii nuntiandi. He wanted catechesis, especially that directed at children and young people, to be the theme of the IV General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops, held during the month of October 1977, in which I myself had the joy of participating.

3.contenido: 3. At the conclusion of the Synod, the Fathers delivered to the Pope a very rich documentation, which included the various interventions made during the Assembly, the conclusions of the working groups, the Message that with their consent they had addressed to the people of God, and above all the imposing series of "Propositions" in which they expressed their opinion about many aspects of catechesis at the current time.

4.contenido: 4. In this same climate of faith and hope I address you today, Venerable Brothers, beloved sons and daughters, this Apostolic Exhortation. On such a broad topic, she will only deal with some more current and decisive aspects, to corroborate the fruits of the Synod. It substantially takes into consideration the reflections that Pope Paul VI had prepared, making extensive use of the documents left by the Synod. Pope John Paul I – whose zeal and qualities as a catechist have caused us so much amazement – ​​had collected them and was preparing to publish them at the moment when he was unexpectedly called by God. He has given all of us the example of a catechesis based on what is essential and at the same time popular, made of simple gestures and words, capable of reaching hearts. I therefore assume the inheritance of these two Pontiffs, to respond to the request of the Bishops, expressly formulated at the end of the IV General Assembly of the Synod and accepted by Pope Paul VI in his closing speech. I also do it to fulfill one of the main duties of my apostolic office. Catechesis has always been a central concern in my ministry as a priest and bishop.

5.contenido: 5. The IV General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops has greatly insisted on the Christocentrism of all authentic catechesis. We can point out here the two meanings of the word that are neither opposed nor exclusive, but rather related and complementary.

6.contenido: 6. In catechesis, Christocentrism also means that, through it, not one's own doctrine or that of another teacher is transmitted, but the teaching of Jesus Christ, the Truth that He communicates or, more precisely, the Truth that He is. So it must be said that in catechesis what is taught is Christ, the incarnate Word and Son of God and everything else in reference to Him; The only one who teaches is Christ, and anyone else does so to the extent that he is his spokesman, allowing Christ to teach through his mouth. The constant concern of every catechist, whatever his responsibility in the Church, must be to communicate, through his teaching and his behavior, the doctrine and life of Jesus. He will not try to fix on himself, on his personal opinions and attitudes, the attention and adherence of the one he catechizes; He will not try to instill his personal opinions and choices as if they expressed the doctrine and life lessons of Christ. Every catechist should be able to apply to himself the mysterious phrase of Jesus: "My doctrine is not mine, but His who sent me." This is what Saint Paul does when addressing a question of primary importance: "I have received from the Lord what I have transmitted to you." What assiduous contact with the Word of God transmitted by the Magisterium of the Church, what deep familiarity with Christ and the Father, what spirit of prayer, what self-detachment the catechist must have to be able to say: "My doctrine is not mine"!

7.contenido: 7. This doctrine is not a collection of abstract truths, it is the communication of the living Mystery of God. The quality of Him who teaches in the Gospel and the nature of His teaching surpasses in all things those of the "teachers" in Israel, thanks to the unique union that exists between what He says, does and what He is. It is evident that the Gospels clearly indicate the moments in which Jesus teaches, "Jesus did and taught": in these two verbs that introduce the book of Acts, Saint Luke unites and distinguishes at the same time two dimensions in the mission of Christ.

8.contenido: 8. He who teaches like this deserves the name of Teacher alone. How many times is this title of teacher given to him throughout the entire New Testament and especially in the Gospels! It is evidently the Twelve, the other disciples and the crowds who listen to him who call him "Master" with an accent of admiration, trust and tenderness at the same time. Even the Pharisees and the Sadducees, the Doctors of the Law and the Jews in general, do not refuse this denomination: "Teacher, we would like to see a sign from you"; «Teacher, what good do I have to do to achieve eternal life?» But above all, Jesus himself calls himself Master on particularly solemn and very significant occasions: "You call me Master and Lord, and you say well, because I truly am"; and proclaims the singularity, the unique character of his condition as Master: "Only one is your Master": Christ. It is understandable that, over two thousand years, in all the languages ​​of the earth, men of every condition, race and nation, have given him this title with veneration, repeating in their own way the exclamation of Nicodemus: "you have come as a Teacher from God."

9.contenido: 9. I do not forget, in doing this, that the majesty of Christ who teaches, the coherence and unique persuasive force of his teaching, are only explained because his words, his parables and reasonings can never be separated from his life and his very being. In this sense, the entire life of Christ was a continuous teaching: his silence, his miracles, his gestures, his prayer, his love for man, his predilection for the little ones and the poor, the acceptance of the total sacrifice on the cross for the salvation of the world, his resurrection are the performance of his word and the fulfillment of revelation. So for Christians the Crucifix is ​​one of the most sublime and popular images of Jesus who teaches.

10.contenido: 10. The image of Christ who teaches had been impressed on the minds of the Twelve and the first disciples, and the motto "Go and make disciples of all nations" guided their entire lives. Saint John testifies to this in his Gospel, when he relates the words of Jesus: «I no longer call you servants, because the servant does not know what his master is doing; But I tell you friends, because everything I heard from my Father I have made known to you. It is not they who have chosen to follow Jesus, but it is Jesus who has chosen them, who has kept them and established them, already before their Passover, so that they would go and bear fruit and so that their fruit would remain. For this reason, after the resurrection, he formally entrusted them with the mission of making disciples of all people.

11.contenido: 11. The Apostles are quick to share the ministry of the apostolate with others. They pass on the mission of teaching to their successors. They also entrust it to the deacons from their institution: Stephen, "full of grace and power", does not stop teaching, moved by the wisdom of the Spirit. The Apostles associate in their task of teaching "other" disciples; and even simple Christians scattered by persecution went everywhere preaching the word. Saint Paul is the quintessential herald of this announcement, from Antioch to Rome, where the last image we have of him according to the book of Acts is that of a man "who freely teaches what concerns the Lord Jesus Christ." His numerous letters expand and deepen his teaching. Likewise, the letters of Peter, John, James and Jude are so many testimonies of the catechesis of the apostolic era.

12.contenido: 12. The Church continues this teaching mission of the Apostles and their first collaborators. Becoming a disciple of the Lord day by day, she has rightly been called "Mother and Teacher." From Clement Romanus to Origen, notable works came to light in the post-apostolic age. Later an impressive fact is recorded: Bishops and Pastors, the most prestigious ones, especially in the third and fourth centuries, considered teaching or writing catechetical treatises as an important part of their episcopal ministry. It is the time of Cyril of Jerusalem and John Chrysostom, of Ambrose and Augustine, in which works emerge from the pens of so many Fathers of the Church that continue to be models for us.

13.contenido: 13. The ministry of catechesis always draws new energies from the Councils. In this regard, the Council of Trent constitutes an example that must be highlighted: in its constitutions and decrees it gave priority to catechesis; It gave rise to the "Roman catechism" that also bears his name and constitutes a work of the first order, a summary of Christian doctrine and traditional theology for the use of priests; He promoted a notable organization of catechesis in the Church; He awakened in the clerics the awareness of their duties in relation to catechetical teaching; and, thanks to the work of holy theologians such as Saint Charles Borromeo, Saint Robert Bellarmine or Saint Peter Canisius, it gave rise to catechisms, true models for that time. May the Second Vatican Council inspire a similar impulse and work in our days!

14.contenido: 14. It is evident, above all, that catechesis has always been a sacred duty and an imprescriptible right for the Church. On the one hand, it is undoubtedly a duty that has its origin in a command from the Lord and concerns above all those who in the New Alliance receive the call to the ministry of Pastors. On the other hand, one can also speak of right: from the theological point of view, everyone baptized by the very fact of his baptism, has the right to receive from the Church a teaching and formation that allows him to begin a truly Christian life; From the perspective of human rights, every human person has the right to seek religious truth and to adhere fully to it, free from "all coercion on the part of individuals as well as social groups and any human power whatsoever, so that, in this matter, no one is forced to act against his conscience or is prevented from acting... in accordance with it."

15.contenido: 15. The second lesson refers to the very place of catechesis in the pastoral projects of the Church. The more capable it is, on a local or universal scale, of giving priority to catechesis "above other works and initiatives whose results could be more spectacular", the more the Church will find in catechesis a consolidation of its internal life as a community of believers and of its external activity as missionary. At the end of the 20th century, God and events, which are so many calls on his part, invite the Church to renew its confidence in catechetical action as an absolutely primary task of its mission. It is invited to devote its best resources in men and energy to catechesis, without sparing effort, fatigue and material means, to better organize it and train qualified personnel. There is not a mere human calculation in this, but an attitude of faith. And an attitude of faith is always directed towards fidelity to God, who never stops responding.

16.contenido: 16. Third lesson: catechesis has always been, and will continue to be, a work for which the entire Church must feel and want to be responsible. But its members have different responsibilities, derived from each one's mission. Pastors, precisely by virtue of their office, have, at different levels, the highest responsibility in the promotion, orientation and coordination of catechesis. The Pope, for his part, is deeply aware of the primary responsibility that falls to him in this field: he finds in it reasons for pastoral concern, but above all for joy and hope. Priests, men and women religious have a privileged field there for their apostolate. At another level, parents have a unique responsibility. The teachers, the various ministers of the Church, the catechists and, on the other hand, those responsible for the media of social communication, all of them have, to varying degrees, very precise responsibilities in this formation of the conscience of the believer, an important formation for the life of the Church, and which has an impact on the life of society itself. One of the best fruits of the General Assembly of the Synod dedicated entirely to catechesis would be to awaken, throughout the Church and in each of its sectors, a living and operating awareness of this differentiated but common responsibility.

17.contenido: 17. Finally, catechesis needs to continually renew itself in a certain lengthening of its very concept, in its methods, in the search for an adapted language, in the use of new means of transmitting the message. This renewal does not always have equal value, and the Fathers of the Synod have realistically recognized, along with undeniable progress in the vitality of catechetical activity and promising initiatives, the limitations or even the "deficiencies" of what has been carried out to date. These limits are particularly serious when they compromise the integrity of the content. The "Message to the People of God" precisely emphasized that, for catechesis, "routine repetition, which opposes all change, on the one hand, and thoughtless improvisation that lightly approaches problems, on the other, are equally dangerous." Routine repetition leads to stagnation, lethargy and, ultimately, paralysis. Thoughtless improvisation engenders confusion in those catechized and in their parents, when it comes to children, it causes deviations of all kinds, ruptures and finally the total ruin of the unity. It is necessary that the Church give proof today - as it knew how to do in other periods of its history - of evangelical wisdom, courage and fidelity, seeking and opening new paths and perspectives for catechetical teaching.

18.contenido: 18. Catechesis cannot be dissociated from the set of pastoral and missionary activities of the Church. It has, however, something specific of its own about which the IV General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops, in its preparatory work and throughout its celebration, has often questioned itself. The issue is also of interest to public opinion, inside and outside the Church.

19.contenido: 19. The peculiarity of Catechesis, distinct from the first proclamation of the Gospel that brought about conversion, pursues the double objective of maturing the initial faith and of educating the true disciple through a deeper and more systematic knowledge of the person and message of Our Lord Jesus Christ. But in catechetical practice, this exemplary order must take into account the fact that sometimes the first evangelization has not taken place. A certain number of children baptized in their childhood arrive at parish catechesis without having received any initiation in the faith, and without yet having any explicit and personal adhesion to Jesus Christ, but only the capacity to believe placed in them by baptism and the presence of the Holy Spirit; and the prejudices of a non-Christian family environment or the positivist spirit of education quickly create some reluctance. To these it is necessary to add other children, not baptized, for whom their parents do not accept religious education until late: for practical reasons, their catechumenal stage will take place largely during ordinary catechesis. Furthermore, many pre-adolescents and adolescents, who have been baptized and who have systematically received catechesis as well as the sacraments, hesitate for a long time whether or not to commit their lives to Jesus Christ, when they do not worry about avoiding religious formation in the name of their freedom. Finally, adults themselves are not immune to temptations to doubt or abandon faith, as a result of a notoriously incredulous environment. That is to say, "catechesis" must often be concerned, not only with nourishing and teaching faith, but with continually arousing it with the help of grace, with opening the heart, with converting, with preparing a global adhesion to Jesus Christ in those who are still on the threshold of faith. This concern partially inspires the tone, language and method of catechesis.

20.contenido: 20. The specific purpose of catechesis is not only to develop, with the help of God, a still initial faith, to fully promote and daily nourish the Christian life of the faithful of all ages. In effect, it is about making the germ of faith grow, at the level of knowledge and life, sown by the Holy Spirit with the first announcement and transmitted effectively through baptism.

21.contenido: 21. In his closing speech at the IV General Assembly of the Synod, Pope Paul VI congratulated himself by "noticing that everyone has pointed out the great need for an organic and well-ordered catechesis, since this vital reflection on the very mystery of Christ is what mainly distinguishes Catechesis from all other forms of presenting the Word of God."

22.contenido: 22. It is useless to insist on orthopraxis to the detriment of orthodoxy: Christianity is inseparably one and the other. Firm and thoughtful convictions lead to brave and confident action; The effort to educate the faithful to live today as disciples of Christ calls for and facilitates the deeper discovery of the Mystery of Christ in the history of salvation.

23.contenido: 23. Catechesis is intrinsically linked to all liturgical and sacramental action, because it is in the sacraments and especially in the Eucharist where Jesus Christ acts fully for the transformation of men.

24.contenido: 24. Catechesis, finally, has an intimate connection with the responsible action of the Church and Christians in the world. Everyone who has adhered to Jesus Christ by faith and strives to consolidate this faith through catechesis, needs to live it in communion with those who have taken the same step. Catechesis runs the risk of becoming sterilized if a community of faith and Christian life does not welcome the catechumen in a certain phase of his catechesis. That is why the ecclesial community, at all levels, is doubly responsible with respect to catechesis: it has the responsibility of attending to the formation of its members, but also the responsibility of welcoming them into an environment where they can live, as fully as possible, what they have learned.

25.contenido: 25. Thus, thanks to catechesis, the evangelical kerygma - the first proclamation full of ardor that one day transformed man and led him to the decision to give himself to Jesus Christ by faith - deepens little by little, develops in its implicit corollaries, explained through a discourse that is also directed at reason, oriented towards Christian practice in the Church and in the world. All this is no less evangelical than the kerygma, even though some say that catechesis would necessarily rationalize, aridize and finally kill what is most alive, spontaneous and vibrant in the kerygma. The truths that are deepened in catechesis are the same ones that made an impact on the heart of man when he heard them for the first time. The fact of knowing them better, far from dulling or exhausting them, should make them even more stimulating and decisive for life.

26.contenido: 26. Catechesis being a moment or an aspect of evangelization, its content cannot be other than that of the entire evangelization: the same message "Good News of salvation" heard a thousand times and accepted from the heart, is incessantly deepened in catechesis through reflection and systematic study; through an increasingly compromising awareness of its repercussions on each person's personal life; through its insertion into the organic and harmonious whole that is Christian existence in society and in the world.

27.contenido: 27. Catechesis will always draw its content from the living source of the Word of God, transmitted through Tradition and Scripture, given that "Tradition and Scripture constitute the sacred deposit of the Word of God, entrusted to the Church", as the Second Vatican Council recalled when wishing that "the ministry of the word, which includes pastoral preaching, catechesis, all Christian instruction... receives healthy nourishment from the word of Scripture and through it bears fruits of holiness.

28.contenido: 28. A privileged expression of the living heritage that they have received in custody is found in the Creed or, more specifically, in the Symbols that, at crucial moments, collected in happy synthesis the faith of the Church. For centuries, an important element of catechesis was precisely the “traditio Symboli” ( [+[0]+] ), followed by the delivery of the Sunday prayer. This expressive rite has been reintroduced in our days in the initiation of catechumens. Shouldn't we find a more specifically adapted use to mark this stage, the most important of all, in which a new disciple of Jesus Christ accepts with full lucidity and courage the content of what he will seriously delve into later?

29.contenido: 29. The Supreme Pontiff himself has recalled, in the third chapter of his Apostolic Exhortation Evangelii nuntiandi, "the essential content, the living substance" of evangelization. It is necessary for catechesis itself to keep in mind each of the elements and the living synthesis in which they have been integrated.

30.contenido: 30. Regarding the content of catechesis, three important points must be highlighted in our days.

31.contenido: 31. Hence this second observation: it is possible that in the current situation of catechesis, reasons of method or pedagogy advise organizing the communication of the riches of the content of catechesis in one way rather than another. For the rest, integrity does not dispense with balance or the organic and hierarchical character, thanks to which the truths that are taught, the norms that are transmitted and the paths of the Christian life that are indicated will be given the respective importance that corresponds to them. It may also happen that certain language proves preferable to transmit this content to a certain person or group of people. The choice would be valid to the extent that it does not depend on theories or prejudices that are more or less subjective and marked by a certain ideology, but rather is inspired by the humble desire to better adjust to a content that must remain intact. The method and language used must remain truly instruments for communicating the whole and not a part of the "words of eternal life" or the "way of life."

32.contenido: 32. The great movement, certainly inspired by the Spirit of Jesus, which, for a certain number of years, has led the Catholic Church to seek with other Churches or Christian confessions the reestablishment of the perfect unity desired by the Lord, leads me to speak of the ecumenical character of catechesis. This movement gained full prominence at the Second Vatican Council, and, since the Council, it has gained importance in the Church, materialized in an impressive series of events and initiatives, known to everyone.

33.contenido: 33. In situations of religious pluralism, the Bishops may deem appropriate, or even necessary, certain experiences of collaboration in the field of catechesis between Catholics and other Christians, as a complement to the usual catechesis that, in any case, Catholics must receive. Such experiences find their theological foundation in the elements common to all Christians. But the communion of faith between Catholics and other Christians is not complete or perfect; Furthermore, there are, in certain cases, profound divergences. Consequently, this ecumenical collaboration is by its nature limited: it should never mean a "reduction" to the common minimum. Furthermore, catechesis does not consist only of teaching doctrine, but of initiating the entire Christian life, participating fully in the sacraments of the Church. Hence the need, where there is an experience of ecumenical collaboration in the field of catechesis, to ensure that the formation of Catholics is well ensured in the Catholic Church with regard to doctrine and Christian life.

34.contenido: 34. Another observation must be added here that is situated in the same direction although from a different perspective. It sometimes happens that state schools make books available to students, in which religions, including Catholicism, are presented for cultural, historical, moral and literary purposes. An objective presentation of historical facts, of the different religions and Christian confessions can contribute to a better mutual understanding. In this case, everything possible will be done to ensure that the presentation is truly objective, protected from ideological and political systems or alleged scientific prejudices that would distort its true meaning. In any case, these manuals should not be considered as catechetical works: they lack the testimony of believers who expose the faith to other believers, and an understanding of the Christian mysteries and what is specifically Catholic, all of this drawn from the depths of the faith.

35.contenido: 35. The theme indicated by my Predecessor, Paul VI, for the IV General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops was about "catechesis in our time with special attention to children and young people." The rise of young people is undoubtedly the richest fact of hope and at the same time of concern for a good part of the world today. In some countries, especially those in the Third World, more than half of the population is under the age of twenty-five or thirty. This means that millions and millions of children and young people are preparing for their future as adults. And it is not only the numerical factor: recent events, and the daily chronicle itself, tell us that this countless multitude of young people, although dominated here and there by uncertainty and fear, or seduced by drug evasion and indifference, even tempted by nihilism and violence, nevertheless constitutes for the most part the great force that, among many risks, proposes to build the civilization of the future.

36.contenido: 36. A frequently highlighted moment is that in which the young child receives from his parents and the family environment the first rudiments of catechesis, which may be nothing more than a simple revelation from the heavenly Father, good and provident, to whom he learns to direct his heart. The very brief prayers that the child will learn to stammer will be the beginning of a loving dialogue with that hidden God, whose Word he will begin to hear later. As Christian parents we would never insist too much on this early initiation, through which the child's faculties are integrated into a vital relationship with God: a capital work that requires great love and deep respect for the child, who has the right to a simple and true presentation of the Christian faith.

37.contenido: 37. Soon there will come, in the school and in the church, in the parish or in the spiritual assistance received in the Catholic school or in the state institute, at the same time as the opening to a broader social circle, the moment of a catechesis aimed at introducing the child organically into the life of the Church, also including an immediate preparation for the celebration of the sacraments: didactic catechesis, but aimed at bearing witness to the faith; initial catechism, but not fragmentary, since it must reveal, albeit in an elementary way, all the main mysteries of the faith and their impact on the moral and religious life of the child; catechism that gives meaning to the sacraments, but at the same time receives from the lived sacraments a vital dimension that prevents it from remaining merely doctrinal, and communicates to the child the joy of being a witness to Christ in his or her life environment.

38.contenido: 38. Then come puberty and adolescence, with the greatness and risks that that age presents. It is the moment of discovery of oneself and one's own inner world, the moment of generous projects, the moment in which the feeling of love arises, as well as the biological impulses of sexuality, of the desire to be together; moment of particularly intense joy, related to the intoxicating discovery of life. But it is also often the age of the deepest questions, of anguishing, even frustrating searches, of distrust of others and of dangerous withdrawals into oneself; sometimes also the age of the first failures and the first bitterness. Catechesis cannot ignore these easily changing aspects of such a delicate period of life. A catechesis capable of leading the adolescent to a review of his or her own life and dialogue may be decisive, a catechesis that does not ignore its major themes, “the donation of self, faith, love and its mediation which is sexuality.” The revelation of Jesus Christ as a friend, as a guide and as a model, admirable and yet imitable; the revelation of his message that answers fundamental questions; the revelation of the Plan of love of Christ the Savior as the incarnation of the only true love and the only possibility of uniting men, all of this can constitute the basis of an authentic education in the faith. And above all, the mysteries of the passion and death of Jesus, to which Saint Paul attributes the merit of his glorious resurrection, will be able to say many things to the conscience and heart of the adolescent and shed light on his first sufferings and those of the world he is discovering.

39.contenido: 39. With the age of youth comes the time for first decisions. Perhaps helped by family members and friends, but in spite of everything alone with himself and his moral conscience, the young man, more and more often and in a more decisive way, must assume his destiny. Good and evil, grace and sin, life and death, will increasingly confront each other within him as moral categories, but also and above all as fundamental options that he will have to make or refuse with lucidity and a sense of responsibility. It is evident that a catechesis that denounces selfishness in the name of generosity, that exposes without simplistics or illusory schematisms the Christian meaning of work, of the common good, of justice and charity, a catechesis on peace among nations, on the promotion of human dignity, development, liberation as presented in recent documents of the Church, will happily complete in the minds of young people a good catechesis of properly religious realities, which It must never be neglected. Catechesis then takes on considerable importance, because it is the moment in which the gospel can be presented, understood and accepted as capable of giving meaning to life and, consequently, of inspiring otherwise inexplicable attitudes: renunciation, detachment, meekness, justice, commitment, reconciliation, a sense of the Absolute and the invisible, etc., all of them traits that will allow this young man to be identified among his peers as a disciple of Jesus Christ.

40.contenido: 40. It is consoling to see that, during the IV General Assembly of the Synod and throughout the years that have followed, the Church has widely shared this concern: How to impart catechesis to children and young people? May God grant that the attention thus awakened may last a long time in the conscience of the Church! In that sense, the Synod has been precious for the entire Church, striving to outline with the greatest possible precision the complex face of today's youth; by showing that this youth uses a language into which it is necessary to know how to translate, with patience and good sense, without betraying it, the message of Jesus Christ; by demonstrating that, despite appearances, this youth has, even if confusingly, not only the availability and openness, but also a true desire to know "Jesus, called Christ"; by revealing, finally, that the work of catechesis, if it is to be carried out with rigor and seriousness, is today more arduous and tiring than ever because of the obstacles and difficulties of all kinds that it encounters, but it is also more comforting than ever because of the depth of the responses it receives from children and young people. There is a treasure that the Church can and should count on in the years to come.

41.contenido: 41. These are above all children and young people who are physically or mentally handicapped. These have the right to know like other contemporaries the "mystery of faith." As the difficulties they encounter are greater, the efforts of them and their educators are more meritorious. It is a source of joy to see that Catholic organizations especially dedicated to handicapped young people were kind enough to contribute to the Synod their experience in the matter, and took from the Synod a renewed desire to better confront this important problem. They deserve to be strongly encouraged in this task.

42.contenido: 42. My thoughts then turn to the children and young people, increasingly numerous, born and educated in a non-Christian home, or at least not practicing, but eager to know the Christian faith. They must be assured adequate catechesis so that they can believe in the faith and live it progressively, despite the lack of support, perhaps despite the opposition they encounter in their family and in their environment.

43.contenido: 43. Continuing the series of recipients of catechesis, I cannot help but highlight now one of the most constant concerns of the Fathers of the Synod, imposed with vigor and urgency by the experiences that are taking place throughout the world: it is the central problem of the catechesis of adults. This is the primary form of catechesis because it is directed at people who have the greatest responsibilities and the ability to live the Christian message in its fully developed form. The Christian community could not carry out permanent catechesis without the direct and experienced participation of adults, whether they are recipients or promoters of catechetical activity. The world in which young people are called to live and bear witness to the faith that catechesis wants to deepen and strengthen, is governed by adults: their faith should equally be illuminated, stimulated or renewed incessantly in order to penetrate the temporal realities for which they are responsible. Thus, to be effective, catechesis must be permanent and it would certainly be in vain if it stopped precisely at the threshold of mature age since, although certainly in another form, it proves no less necessary for adults.

44.contenido: 44. Among these adults who need catechesis, our pastoral and missionary concern is directed to those who, born and educated in regions not yet Christianized, have not been able to deepen the Christian doctrine that one day the circumstances of life made them find; to those who in their childhood received a catechism proportionate to that age, but who later distanced themselves from all religious practice and find themselves in mature age with rather childish religious knowledge; to those who resent a catechesis that is undoubtedly early, but poorly oriented or poorly assimilated; to those who, even having been born in Christian countries, even within a sociologically Christian framework, were never educated in their faith and, as adults, are true catechumens.

45.contenido: 45. Thus, adults of any age, including the elderly – who deserve special attention given their experience and problems – are recipients of catechesis just like children, adolescents and young people. We should also talk about emigrants, people marginalized by modern evolution, those who live in the neighborhoods of large metropolises, often devoid of churches, premises and adequate structures. For all of them I want to express my hope that initiatives aimed at their Christian formation with the appropriate instruments ([+[0]+]) will multiply, so that many adults can make up for the insufficiencies or deficiencies of catechesis, or harmoniously complete, at a higher level, what they received in childhood, or even enrich themselves in this field to the point of being able to help others more seriously.

46.contenido: 46. ​​From the oral teaching of the Apostles to the letters that circulated among the Churches and even the most modern means, catechesis has not ceased to seek the methods and means most appropriate to its mission, with the active participation of the communities, under the impulse of the Pastors. This effort must continue.

47.contenido: 47. I am also thinking of various moments of great importance in which catechesis fully finds its place: for example, diocesan, regional or national pilgrimages, which are more profitable if they are focused on a theme wisely chosen from the life of Christ, the Virgin and the Saints; the traditional missions, so often abandoned in excessive haste, and which are irreplaceable for a periodic and vigorous renewal of the Christian life "they must be resumed and renewed"; biblical circles, which must go beyond exegesis to make the Word of God live; the meetings of the base ecclesial communities, to the extent that they adhere to the criteria set forth in the Apostolic Exhortation Evangelii nuntiandi. I also want to remember the groups of young people that in certain regions, with different denominations and physiognomies - but with the same goal of making Jesus Christ known and living the Gospel - multiply and flourish as in a very comforting spring for the Church: Catholic action groups, charitable groups, prayer groups, Christian reflection groups, etc. These groups raise great hopes for the Church of tomorrow. But in the name of Jesus I conjure the young people who form them, their leaders and the priests who consecrate to them the best of their ministry: do not for the world allow that in these groups, privileged occasions of encounter, rich in so many values ​​of youthful friendship and solidarity, of joy and enthusiasm, of reflection on facts and things, a true study of Christian doctrine is lacking. In that case they would expose themselves - and the danger, unfortunately, has been amply verified - to disappointing their members and the Church itself.

48.contenido: 48. This observation is even more valid for the catechesis that is carried out within the liturgical framework and specifically in the liturgical assembly: respecting the specificity and the proper rhythm of this framework, the homily retraces the itinerary of faith proposed by the catechesis and leads it to its natural perfection; At the same time, it encourages the disciples of the Lord to undertake their spiritual journey each day in truth, adoration and thanksgiving. In this sense it can be said that catechetical pedagogy finds, in turn, its source and its plenitude in the Eucharist within the complete horizon of the liturgical year. Preaching centered on biblical texts must then, in its own way, facilitate the faithful becoming familiar with all the mysteries of faith and the norms of Christian life. Great attention must be paid to the homily: neither too long, nor too short, always carefully prepared, substantial and appropriate, and reserved for authorized ministers. This homily must have its place in every Sunday or festive Eucharist, and also in the celebration of baptisms, penitential liturgies, marriages, and funerals. This is one of the benefits of the renewed liturgy.

49.contenido: 49. In the midst of this set of ways and means – every activity of the Church has a catechetical dimension – the works of catechism, far from losing their essential importance, acquire new importance. One of the most interesting aspects of the current flourishing of catechesis consists of the renewal and multiplication of catechetical books that in the Church has been verified a little everywhere. Numerous and very successful works have seen the light, and they constitute a true wealth at the service of catechetical teaching. But we must also recognize, with honesty and humility, that this flowering and this wealth have brought with it trials and publications that are misleading and detrimental to young people and to the life of the Church. Quite often, here and there, in order to find the most suitable language or to be up to date with regard to pedagogical methods, certain catechetical works disorient young people and even adults, either by the omission, conscious or unconscious, of essential elements to the faith of the Church, or by the excessive importance given to certain topics to the detriment of others, or above all by a very horizontalist global vision, not in accordance with the teaching of the Magisterium of the Church.

50.contenido: 50. All those who assume the heavy task of preparing these catechetical instruments, and even more so the text of the catechisms, cannot do so without the approval of the Pastors who have the authority to give it, nor without drawing as much inspiration as possible from the General Directory of Catechesis, which continues to be the standard of reference.

51.contenido: 51. The age and intellectual development of Christians, their degree of ecclesial and spiritual maturity and many other personal circumstances require that catechesis adopt very diverse methods to achieve its specific purpose: education in the faith. This variety is also required, on a more general level, by the socio-cultural environment in which the Church carries out its catechetical work.

52.contenido: 52. The first general question that arises concerns the risk and temptation of improperly mixing catechetical teaching with ideological perspectives, openly or covertly, especially of a political-social nature, or with personal political options. When these perspectives predominate over the central message to be transmitted, to the point of obscuring it and relegating it to a secondary level, even to the point of using it for their own purposes, then catechesis is distorted at its roots. The Synod has rightly insisted on the need for catechesis to remain above divergent unilateral tendencies – to avoid “dichotomies” – even in the field of theological interpretations given to such questions. The guideline that must be sought to follow is Revelation, as transmitted by the universal Magisterium of the Church in its solemn or ordinary form. This Revelation is that of a creator and redeeming God, whose Son, having come among men in flesh, not only enters the personal history of each man, but also into human history, becoming its center. This is, therefore, the Revelation of a radical change of man and the universe, of everything that forms the fabric of human existence, under the influence of the Good News of Jesus Christ. A catechesis understood in this way surpasses all formalist moralism, even when it includes true Christian morality. It mainly surpasses all temporal, social or political messianism. Aim to reach the bottom of the man.

53.contenido: 53. I now address a second issue. As I recently told the members of the Bible Commission, "the term "acculturation" or "inculturation", in addition to being a beautiful neologism, expresses very well one of the components of the great mystery of the Incarnation." Of catechesis, as of evangelization in general, we can say that it is called to bring the force of the gospel to the heart of culture and cultures. To do this, catechesis will seek to know these cultures and their essential components; You will learn its most significant expressions, you will respect your own values ​​and riches. Only in this way can knowledge of the hidden mystery be offered to such cultures and help them to bring forth from their own living tradition original expressions of Christian life, celebration and thought. Two things will often be remembered:

54.contenido: 54. Another question of method concerns the valorization, through catechetical teaching, of the valid elements of popular piety. I think of the devotions that in certain regions the faithful people practice with a moving fervor and righteousness of intention, even when in many aspects the faith on which they rely must be purified, or even rectified. I think of certain sentences that are easy to understand and that so many simple people like to repeat. I think of certain acts of piety practiced with a sincere desire to do penance or to please the Lord. In most of these prayers or practices, along with elements that must be eliminated, there are others that, well used, could serve very well to advance the knowledge of the mystery of Christ or his message: the love and mercy of God, the Incarnation of Christ, his redeeming cross and his resurrection, the action of the Spirit in each Christian and in the Church, the mystery of the afterlife, the practice of the evangelical virtues, the presence of the Christian in the world, etc. And why would we have to use non-Christian – even anti-Christian – elements, refusing to rely on elements that, although in need of revision and rectification, have something Christian at their root?

55.contenido: 55. The last methodological issue that should at least be emphasized – it was referred to more than once in the Synod – is memorization. The beginnings of Christian catechesis, which coincided with an eminently oral civilization, made extensive use of memorization. And catechesis has known a long tradition of learning the main truths by memory. We all know that this method can present certain drawbacks: not the least of which is that it leads to insufficient assimilation, sometimes almost zero, reducing all knowledge to formulas that are repeated without having penetrated them. These drawbacks, together with the diverse characteristics of our civilization, have led here or there to the almost total suppression - definitive, unfortunately, according to some - of memorization in catechesis. And yet, on the occasion of the IV General Assembly of the Synod, very authoritative voices have been heard to rebalance with good judgment the part of reflection and spontaneity, of dialogue and silence, of written works and memory. On the other hand, certain cultures highly value memorization.

56.contenido: 56. We live in a difficult world where the anguish of seeing man's best achievements escape him and turn against him, creates a climate of uncertainty. It is in this world where catechesis must help Christians to be, for their joy and for the service of all, "light" and "salt." This requires that catechesis gives them firmness in their own identity and that they constantly overcome the hesitations, uncertainties and unrest of the environment. Among many other difficulties, which are so many challenges for faith, I highlight some to help catechesis overcome them.

57.contenido: 57. There was a lot of talk, a few years ago, about a secularized world, about a post-Christian era. Fashion passes... But a deep reality remains. Today's Christians must be trained to live in a world that largely ignores God or that, in religious matters, instead of a demanding and fraternal dialogue, stimulating for all, very often falls into a leveling indifferentism, when it does not remain in a contemptuous attitude of "suspicion" in the name of its progress in matters of scientific "explanations." To "enter" this world, to offer everyone a "dialogue of salvation" where each one feels respected in his fundamental dignity, that of seeker of God, we need a catechesis that teaches the young and adults of our communities to remain lucid and coherent in their faith, to serenely affirm their Christian and Catholic identity, to "see the invisible" and to adhere in such a way to the absolute of God that they can bear witness to Him in a materialistic civilization that he denies it.

58.contenido: 58. The irreducible originality of Christian identity has as a corollary and condition a no less original pedagogy of faith. Among the numerous and prestigious sciences of man that have progressed enormously in our days, pedagogy is certainly one of the most important. The achievements of the other sciences – biology, psychology, sociology – offer valuable contributions. The science of education and the art of teaching are the subject of continuous rethinking with a view to better adaptation or greater effectiveness, with otherwise uneven results.

59.contenido: 59. A problem, similar to the previous one, is that of language. Everyone knows how hot this topic is. Isn't it also paradoxical to note that contemporary studies, in the field of communication, semantics and the science of symbols, for example, give notable importance to language; But, on the other hand, is language used abusively today in the service of ideological mystification, the massification of thought and the reduction of man to the state of an object?

60.contenido: 60. A very subtle challenge sometimes comes from the very way of understanding faith. Certain contemporary philosophical schools, which seem to exert great influence on some theological currents and, through them, on pastoral practice, willingly emphasize that the fundamental human attitude is that of an endless search, a search that never reaches its object. In theology, this way of seeing things will state very categorically that faith is not a certainty but a question, it is not a clarity but a leap into the darkness.

61.contenido: 61. In this context, it seems important to me that the correlation between catechesis and theology is well understood.

62.contenido: 62. Now, dear Brothers and Sons, I would like my words, conceived as a serious and ardent exhortation of my ministry as Pastor of the universal Church, to inflame your hearts in the manner of Saint Paul's letters to his companions of the Gospel Titus and Timothy, in the manner of Saint Augustine when he wrote to the deacon Deogracias, discouraged about the joy of catechizing. Yes, I want to sow prodigally in the hearts of all those responsible, so numerous and diverse, for religious teaching and training in life according to the Gospel, courage, hope and enthusiasm!

63.contenido: 63. I address first of all to you, my Brother Bishops: the Second Vatican Council already explicitly reminded you of your task in the catechetical field, and the Fathers of the IV General Assembly of the Synod expressly underlined it.

64.contenido: 64. As for you, priests, here you have a field in which you are the immediate collaborators of your Bishops. The Council has called you "educators of the faith": How can you be more fully than by dedicating the best of your efforts to the growth of your communities in faith? Whether you have a parish position or are chaplains in a school, institute or university, whether you are responsible for pastoral care at any level or animators of small or large communities, but above all of youth groups, the Church expects you to leave nothing undone with a view to a well-structured and well-oriented catechetical work. The deacons and other ministers who may be around you are your natural collaborators. All believers have the right to catechesis; All pastors have the duty to impart it. We will always ask the civil authorities to respect the freedom of catechetical teaching; To you, ministers of Jesus Christ, I beg you with all my strength: do not allow the faithful to be left without catechism due to a certain lack of zeal, as a consequence of some inopportune, preconceived idea. That it cannot be said: "the little ones ask for bread and there is no one to break it for them."

65.contenido: 65. Many male and female religious families were born for the Christian education of children and young people, mainly the most abandoned. In the course of history, religious men and women have found themselves very involved in the catechetical activity of the Church, carrying out particularly suitable and effective work. At a time when we want to intensify the links between religious and pastors and, consequently, the active presence of religious communities and their members in the pastoral projects of local Churches, I wholeheartedly urge you, who by virtue of religious consecration must be even more available to serve the Church, to prepare yourselves as best as possible for the catechetical task, according to the different vocations of your institutes and the missions that have been entrusted to you, taking this everywhere. concern. May communities dedicate the maximum of their capacities and possibilities to the specific work of catechesis!

66.contenido: 66. On behalf of the entire Church I want to thank you, parish catechists, men and, in even greater numbers, women, who throughout the world have dedicated yourselves to the religious education of numerous generations of children. Your activity, often humble and hidden, but always exercised with ardent and generous zeal, is an eminent form of secular apostolate, particularly important where, for various reasons, children and young people do not receive adequate religious formation in their homes. Indeed, how many of us have received from people like you the first notions of catechism and preparation for the sacrament of reconciliation, for first communion and for confirmation? The IV General Assembly of the Synod has not forgotten you. With it I encourage you to continue your collaboration in the life of the Church.

67.contenido: 67. I now want to evoke the concrete framework in which all these catechists usually act, returning even more synthetically to the "places" of catechesis, some of which have already been evoked in chapter VI: parish, family, school and movement.

68.contenido: 68. The catechetical action of the family has a peculiar and in a certain sense irreplaceable character, rightly emphasized by the Church, especially by the Second Vatican Council. This education in faith, taught by parents - which must begin from the earliest age of children - is already carried out when family members help each other to grow in faith through their testimony of Christian life, often silent, but persevering throughout a daily existence lived according to the Gospel. It will be more important when, at the pace of family events - such as the reception of the sacraments, the celebration of great liturgical festivals, the birth of a child or the occasion of mourning - an effort is made to explain the Christian or religious content of these events as a family. But it is important to go further: Christian parents must strive to follow and resume in the family environment the more methodical training received in the past. The fact that these truths about the main issues of faith in Christian life are thus transmitted in a family environment impregnated with love and respect will often allow them to leave a decisive and lifelong mark on children. Parents themselves should take advantage of the effort that this imposes on them, because in a catechetical dialogue of this type each one receives and gives.

69.contenido: 69. Next to the family and in collaboration with it, the school offers catechesis non-negligible possibilities. In countries, unfortunately increasingly rare, where it is possible to provide education in the faith within the school framework, the Church has the duty to do it as best as possible. This refers, above all, to the Catholic school: Would it still deserve this name if, even though it stood out for its high level of teaching in secular subjects, there were justified reasons to reproach it for its negligence or deviation in properly religious education? And let it not be said that this will always be given implicitly or indirectly! The very character and deep reason of the Catholic school, the reason why Catholic parents should prefer it, is precisely the quality of the religious teaching integrated into the education of the students. If it is true that Catholic institutions must respect freedom of conscience, that is, avoid burdening it from the outside, due to physical or moral pressures, especially with regard to the religious acts of adolescents, it is no less true that they have the serious duty to offer a religious formation adapted to the often diverse situations of the students, and also to make them understand that God's call to serve him in spirit and in truth, according to the commandments of God and the precepts of the Church, without constraining man, no less obligates him in conscience.

70.contenido: 70. Finally, may the associations, movements and groups of faithful who dedicate themselves to the practice of piety, to the apostolate, to charity and assistance, to the Christian presence in temporal realities receive my word of encouragement. All of them will achieve their own objectives and serve the Church all the better, the more important the space they dedicate, in their internal organization and in their method of action, to a serious religious formation of their members. In this sense, every association of faithful in the Church must be, by definition, an educator of the faith. Thus, the part that corresponds to lay people in catechesis today appears more ostensibly, always under the pastoral direction of their Bishops, as, moreover, the Propositions formulated by the Synod have emphasized on several occasions.

71.contenido: 71. This contribution of the laity, for which we must be acknowledged to the Lord, constitutes at the same time a challenge to our responsibility as Pastors. In effect, these lay catechists must receive careful training for what is, if not a formally instituted ministry, then at least a function of very high importance in the Church. Now, this formation invites us to organize suitable Centers and Institutes, on which the Bishops will maintain constant attention. It is a field in which diocesan, interdiocesan and even national collaboration proves fruitful and fruitful. Here, likewise, is where the material help offered by the more prosperous Churches to their poorer sisters will be able to manifest its greatest effectiveness. In fact, can a Church do anything better for another than helping it grow by itself as a Church?

72.contenido: 72. At the end of this Apostolic Exhortation, the gaze turns to Him who is the inspiring principle of all catechetical work and of those who carry it out: the Spirit of the Father and the Son: the Holy Spirit.

73.contenido: 73. May the Virgin of Pentecost obtain it for us with her intercession. Through a singular vocation, she saw her Son Jesus “grow in wisdom, age, and grace.” In her lap and then listening to her, throughout the hidden life in Nazareth, this Son, who was the Only Begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth, has been formed by her in the human knowledge of the Scriptures and the history of God's plan for his People, in the adoration of the Father. On the other hand, she has been the first of his disciples: first in time, because upon meeting him in the Temple, she receives some lessons from her adolescent Son that she keeps in her heart; the first, above all, because no one has been taught by God in such depth. "Mother and at the same time disciple," Saint Augustine said of her, boldly adding that this was more important to her than the other. Not without reason in the Synodal Hall it was said of Mary that she is "a living catechism", "mother and model of catechists."
